title: Brothers Confrontation
next_chapter_hook: When Chen Ji trembling unfolded the blood-stained cloth, the blurred characters revealed a shocking truth—his father's death might only be the beginning of a much larger chess game.

text.content:
The night wind wailed through the Bamboo Grove, stretching Su Qingyao's departing figure into a slender silhouette. Chen Ji stood at the Cliff of the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain, his robes fluttering violently in the wind. Her tears seemed to still cling to her lashes, and the words "There are things I must do, but I will not betray you" echoed in his ears.

He understood her mission—a secret order from an Inner Sect Elder to investigate Sect Master Ling Yuan's recent peculiar actions. Yet Chen Ji was more acutely aware of what awaited her at the end of this path.

"Brother."

A voice from behind interrupted his thoughts. Chen Ji turned to see Chen Nian slowly walking out from the depths of the Bamboo Grove. Moonlight fell upon him, outlining a face that bore a seventy percent resemblance to their father—the mark of twelve years of shared life.

"You're here." Chen Ji's voice was calm, betraying no emotion, "I've been waiting for you for a long time."

dialogue.content: Chen Nian did not answer immediately. He stopped three steps before Chen Ji, his eyes deep as an abyss under the moonlight. After a long silence, he spoke, his voice low: "Brother, I know you've been investigating Father's death."

text.content:
"So what?" Chen Ji's tone was indifferent, as if discussing something utterly unrelated to himself. His right hand hung at his side, his fingertips unconsciously rubbing against the Tianji Record Fragment hidden in his sleeve—that was his trump card, and his only source of security at this moment.

Chen Nian took a deep breath, as if making some resolute decision: "Brother, before you find out anything, there are things I must tell you myself."

dialogue.content: "I am not your blood brother." Chen Nian's voice was soft, yet it exploded like thunder in the night sky, "I am an orphan Father rescued from the ruins of Linyuan City—that year I was four, pulled out from under collapsed buildings, covered in blood, already unable to speak."

text.content:
The wind suddenly stopped.

Chen Ji felt his heart skip a beat. That question that had haunted him countless nights—why he and Chen Nian looked so alike, why Father always showed a trace of undetectable guilt toward Chen Nian—seemed to have an answer now.

"Continue." He heard his own voice, dry and icy cold.

dialogue.content: Chen Nian's eyes grew slightly red, but he held back his tears: "Three days before Father's death, he called me to his bedside. He told me... told me about the Tianji Record, told me that the one it chose would only be of Chen bloodline, and that I was a being excluded by the Tianji Record."

text.content:
Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply.

The one chosen by the Tianji Record would only be of Chen bloodline—this sentence was like a blunt knife, brutally carving into his heart. What did this mean? It meant Father had known from the start who the Tianji Record would choose, it meant Chen Nian's adoption was no coincidence, it meant...

"What else did Father say?" His voice was cold as a poisoned blade's edge.

dialogue.content: "Father said..." Chen Nian's voice began to tremble, "He said that taking me to Linyuan City back then was to use me to test the Tianji Record's reaction. Because the Tianji Record had no感应 to those without bloodline, he needed to confirm how it would choose after encountering me."

text.content:
From the depths of the Bamboo Grove came a night owl's mournful cry, mournful and prolonged.

Chen Ji finally understood. Father's death was indirectly related to Chen Nian—it was precisely because Father intended to use Chen Nian to test the Tianji Record that it triggered the subsequent series of events. The city's destruction, the black-clad pursuers chasing them brothers that night—all pointed to the same truth.

"So Father's death..." He did not finish, but Chen Nian had already understood his unfinished meaning.

dialogue.content: "Father's death, I indeed cannot escape responsibility." Chen Nian met Chen Ji's eyes directly, without evasion, "But his last words before death were—for me to protect you no matter what. He said you were the Chen family's last hope, and my life belonged to the Chen family as early as twelve years ago."

text.content:
Under the moonlight, two figures stood facing each other. One as tranquil as an abyss, the other as resolute as cold ice. Twelve years of brotherhood, twelve years of depending on each other—all had transformed into sharp blades, cutting through the thin veil of trust between them.

"Brother, how will you dispose of me?" Chen Nian's voice was soft, yet carried a composure that had already transcended life and death.

choice.prompt: Faced with Chen Nian's confession and willingness to accept any outcome, Chen Ji needed to make a choice.

choices.description: The past cannot be changed, but Chen Nian is still the brother who fought beside him. Choose to accept, and face the storms of the future together.
choices.visible_cost: Temporarily suppress the pursuit of truth
choices.visible_reward: Brotherly relationship restored, gaining Chen Nian's absolute loyalty
choices.risk_hint: May miss key clues in investigating the truth of Father's death

text.content:
Chen Ji fell silent for a long time. The night wind rose again, brushing the hair from his forehead, and also brushing away the frost in his eyes.

"Get up." He spoke, his voice still flat, but no longer cold enough to wound, "The ground is cold."

dialogue.content:
Chen Nian was stunned. He raised his head and saw Chen Ji's extended hand—the hand that had tucked blankets over him during countless cold nights, and had also pulled him back from the edge of death in the ruins of Linyuan City.

"Brother..." His voice choked.

choices.description: Father's death cannot remain unclear and unaddressed. Everything Chen Nian knows must be spoken, even if the truth tears apart the affection between brothers.
choices.visible_reward: Gain more clues about father's deathbed truth

text.content: Chen Ji did not reach out his hand. He simply stood there quietly, gazing at Chen Nian kneeling on the ground, his eyes deep and still as two dry wells. 'What else did Father say before he died? Tell me everything, not a single word missing.'

dialogue.content: Chen Nian's expression froze for an instant, but he quickly regained his composure. He drew a blood-stained cloth from his chest and presented it to Chen Ji with both hands: 'This was written by Father before his death. He instructed me to deliver it personally to you, and said... once you read it, you will understand everything.'

choices.description: Truth and falsehood are difficult to distinguish, and hearts are unfathomable. Even if Chen Nian speaks the truth, how do we know this isn't another meticulously crafted deception? We must probe his true intentions.
choices.visible_cost: Exhaust energy in intricate psychological maneuvering
choices.visible_reward: Distinguish truth from falsehood in Chen Nian's words, possibly uncovering hidden third-party forces
choices.risk_hint: If judgment is mistaken, may lose a genuine ally

text.content:
Chen Ji's lips curved slightly upward, but there was no笑意 in his eyes. He walked slowly to Chen Nian and looked down at him: 'Well spoken. But I'm curious—if tonight I stood here not as a Chen bloodline, but as the Tianji Record inheritor?'

Before the words finished, an invisible pressure poured out from him.

dialogue.content: Chen Nian's body shuddered violently, but he did not retreat. Instead, he raised his head and stared directly into Chen Ji's eyes: 'Brother, every word I said is true. As for whether you believe me...' He drew a blood-stained cloth from his chest, 'This was written by Father himself before his death. He ordered me to give it to you when you asked about the truth.'

text.content:
Chen Ji took the cloth. The moment it touched his palm, a familiar scent of blood hit his nose, shocking his heart.

This was Father's blood—he would never mistake it. Twelve years ago, in that great fire, Father had soaked their swaddling clothes with such blood, allowing him and Chen Nian to survive in the ruins.

The characters on the cloth were crooked and slanted, some places already blurred by blood, but several key words could still be made out—'Tianji... choice... not of our kind... its heart must be different...'

Under the moonlight, Chen Ji's gaze suddenly turned sharp. He recognized several characters—'临渊', 'Ling Yuan', 'Tianji Record'. These words, strung together, outlined a truth that made his spine tingle.

'The destruction of Linyuan City... Ling Yuan... the choice of the Tianji Record...' he murmured to himself, his pupils reflecting the blurred characters on the blood-stained cloth, 'So that's how it was... so that's how it is!'

Chen Nian watched him quietly, awaiting his reaction.

choice.prompt: The information on the cloth plunged Chen Ji into deep contemplation. Ling Yuan's sect master, Linyuan City, the Tianji Record... what connection exists between all these?

choices.description: Since Chen Nian has already handed over Father's testament, it shows he harbors no secrets. Share your discoveries with him and jointly analyze this tangled mess.
choices.visible_reward: Gain Chen Nian's insights, possibly discovering overlooked details
choices.risk_hint: If Chen Nian is concealing something, this will expose one's own cards

text.content:
Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, then extended the cloth to Chen Nian, pointing at several blurred characters: 'Look here—'临渊', 'Ling Yuan', and this... doesn't it resemble 'choice'?"

Chen Nian leaned in for a closer look, his brow gradually furrowing: 'Brother, are you suggesting... that Ling Yuan's sect master is connected to Linyuan City's destruction?'

dialogue.content: 'It's not just connected.' A cold light flashed in Chen Ji's eyes, 'What Father means is—Ling Yuan likely knew who the Tianji Record would choose, so he deliberately set a trap in Linyuan City, using your existence to test the Tianji Record's reaction. And that city destruction... was perhaps nothing more than a sacrifice.'

choices.description: The truth is too shocking to let a second person know before complete verification. Even with Chen Nian, one must keep something in reserve.
choices.visible_cost: Lose the opportunity to gain a new perspective
choices.visible_reward: Protect one's reasoning from leaking, maintain information advantage

text.content: Chen Ji tucked the cloth into his sleeve, his face returning to its usual indifferent expression: "Understood. Don't mention this to anyone for now."\n\nChen Nian opened his mouth, as if wanting to say something, but ultimately just nodded: "Rest assured, Brother, I know what's轻重."

text.content:
The night wind blew again, carrying faint spiritual energy fluctuations from afar. Chen Ji frowned—the direction of the Inner Sect Elders' Hall, where Su Qingyao was headed tonight.

"Brother, what's wrong?" Chen Nian noticed his unusual expression.

"Nothing." Chen Ji withdrew his gaze, his eyes holding a complex light as he looked at Chen Nian: "Whether you're Father's biological son or not, you're still my brother whom I raised. From now on, your affairs are my affairs."

dialogue.content: Chen Nian's eyes instantly reddened. He nodded vigorously, voice somewhat choked: "Brother, I owe you too much in this life. No matter what happens in the future, my life, Chen Nian's life, will always be yours."

text.content:
Chen Ji looked at him, his gaze profound. Twelve years ago, that trembling child amidst the ruins had grown into a man he could fight alongside. No matter what his bloodline was, one thing would never change—they were brothers, each other's only reliance in this chaotic world.

"Let's go." Chen Ji turned and walked down the mountain: "Regarding the matter with Ling Yuan, I'll handle it personally. You, go rest first. Starting tomorrow, I have some things for you to do."

Behind him, Chen Nian followed closely. The two figures gradually faded into the moonlight.

When Chen Ji unfolded the blood-stained cloth with trembling hands, a shocking truth emerged from the faint writing—Father's death might merely be the beginning of a much larger chess game. And the line at the bottom of the cloth, almost soaked through with blood, was subtly pointing to a name that sent a chill down Chen Ji's spine...
